title: Canonical vector operations on flat algebra deformation tangent classes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $B$ a commutative $k$-algebra. Use the marked Artinian test category and its square-zero tests $k[V]$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], and the marked flat deformation groupoids and canonical tensor-product base-change relation [def-sfb-marked-flat-algebra-deformations]. Define $T_B$ to be the set of isomorphism classes of $\mathrm{Def}_B(k[k])$ and $[Q]$ the class of $Q$. For a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, a linear map $f:V\to k$, $Q\in\mathrm{Def}_B(k[V])$ and $x\in T_B$, say that $Q$ induces $x$ along $f$ if there is $D\in\mathrm{Def}_B(k[k])$ with $[D]=x$ and a canonical marked base-change map $Q\to D$ above the residue-preserving square-zero map $(a,v)\mapsto(a,f(v))$ [def-sfb-marked-stack-deformations]. For an additive commutative group and $k$-module structure on $T_B$, define the predicate that this is the canonical deformation vector-space structure by the following two requirements. For every dual-number deformation $Q$, $c\in k$ and $y\in T_B$, $c[Q]=y$ if and only if $Q$ induces $y$ along $v\mapsto cv$. For $x,y,z\in T_B$, $x+y=z$ if and only if there is $Q\in\mathrm{Def}_B(k[k\times k])$ inducing $x,y,z$ along the first projection, second projection and addition map, respectively.
